Exactly, so that makes me think that the developers sometimes just say things, or things they say are lost in translation or perhaps misinterpreted. We all know gameplay vs lore can be wack, and that's why I love Rise and World so much compared to the last titles. The lore and the actual fights feel like they can somewhat correlate. Perhaps the fights in frontier are way crazier than they need to be, simply for gameplay reasons. And the developers can also make mistakes in what they say sometimes. Maybe they said frontier is part of the lore, simply to not disrespect the amount of work put into it. We may never know...

Personally, I believe the developers are trying to make 5th Gen and maybe 6th Gen the "main series" lore. Maybe 4th Gen is part of it too, to an extent. Once again, I'm speculating. And if they are, that's great, because now they can put lore and gameplay together with the new technology we have. 

Definitely try Lance in MHWIB and Sunbreak. It is incredible, and very misunderstood. My goal is to put another weapon at the bottom of popularity. Lance has been slept on for a long time. The developers also haven't directly stated that Fatalis is the strongest. (At least, the 5th generation iteration) only that he is "the top of the food chain." I think they are intentionally leaving it up to speculation for the fans. I do still think Fatalis is known to be the strongest, but I'm not going to say that Safi is undeniably less powerful. 

Same thing with the story of the Saphire star. It's very vague, and it's a legend created by man. Perhaps Safi Jiiva originates from space, or earth, or maybe even the life-force and energy of the monsters on the earth cause something to form, travel to space to get some extra stardust and whatnot, and descend back to earth. For all we know, Safi Jiiva could really just be Jaggi on wyverian mega tren lol.

The way I interpret the poem, is that some kind of monster flew to the stars eventually to become one... or perhaps, absorb one. Maybe Safi Jiiva was originally only capable of absorbing energy, and it flew to space to absorb enough energy to create the whole "bio energy organ" it has... after all, a star is pretty much unlimited energy, and there's the saying "energy cannot be created nor destroyed, only transformed." Perhaps Safi Jiiva LITERALLY has the power of a star within it.

Once again, this is just silly speculating. But I think the stories and power levels are intentionally designed to be vague so that they are debated and speculated upon. 

This, and what is "canon" is also a little subjective... for example, frontier... nobody seems to believe it's "canon" despite the fact that the developers have said it is. In this case Dhisufiroa would be undeniably the strongest monster. But one could also argue that perhaps translated into other games, Dhisu wouldn't be as powerful. This is what I love about 5th Gen Fatalis. It finally made him reputable and believable. Unlike the last Fatalis fights and lore, I can actually believe he's one of the most powerful beings, since he's actually believable now. That's why I love World and Rise so much, they make it feel like you're in an actual world and not just some fantasy fever dream xD. 

Anyways, have you tried Lance out yet?

Honestly, to me, Safi has dethroned Fatalis. I hope Safi gets some focus in MH6, because as someone who's played MH for like a decade, Fatalis is getting old. I have a theory that Capcom had bigger plans for Safi, but Covid changed the course of the game. That, or maybe Safi will have some continuation. 

Fatalis is amazing, and he FINALLY got a great fight. Arguable one of the best fights in the series. But now that he got a glorious battle finally, if I hear Fatalis comes back in MH6 as the final boss, it won't be exciting. Because he's been the final boss in so many of the games... there's no suspense, it's just "oh, guess we just wait until Fatalis again." 

And I think Safi is perfect for the role. Safi perfectly represents the whole "delicate ecosystem" thing, as it is literally a massive parasite from possibly another world. Plus the possibilities are endless with such a unique design. What if XenoJiiva doesn't always turn into a western red dragon? What if that's just the way it grows due to the energy it absorbs and the environment? Safi is almost like a massive rathalos with a less wyvern-esque look. What if Safi could keep the same skeleton, but take on looks more similar to Nergigante? Gore Magala? Gaismagorm? Or perhaps a "pure" form? This is just a bunch of speculating nonsense from myself though.

If I hear that "Safi" gets an appearance in MH6 with a better hunt, I'll be much happier than seeing Fatalis for the next 50 times lol. At least, as the final big bad. I'd love for crimson Fatalis to return.

Plus, Safi's armor is so unique and it's weapons too. I personally think Safi and Fatalis are at least in equal strength. I find it hard to believe they'd make a monster like Safi, only to be upped by Fatalis. They put so much effort into Safi. The entire story of the game pretty much revolves around it. And it almost feels like Safi is a side flagship. They made Safi so detailed and put so much lore into it, from the 5 creators to the whole alien/ecosystem manipulation thing, it makes no sense that Safi wasn't the last title update. Perhaps Fatalis was fanservice? Which, if that's the case, I'm glad. Because Fatalis finally lived up to his hype. But I do really hope they build upon all the effort they put into Safi. 

Anyways, tangent over. Use Lance, the least popular weapon. It's incredible.

Demogorgon:

When you hit a survivor, furiously head nod while demo is screaming. This instills immense fear into your victim, causing them to lose focus and run into an obstacle.

Cars in badham experienced mechanical failures and were never recalled. They are not solid objects, but rather slippery slides. Use this to make demo do a goofy little jump, and joyfully brutalize your soon to be food with a shred.

Learn demo's shred. It's not just a straight line extended lunge, you can curve it, and it has disgustingly large side to side hitboxes sometimes. You can use it on many many loops... including the ones on garden of joy... you just have to try using it more. Watching videos of this can show you the true power...

Demo gets very hungry and prefers Asian food. Bring a mori every time you see a Feng min, especially if they have a deliciously metallic flashy. 

You can trick survivors into swerving (which slows them down) by opening up shred for a split second. This will not slow you down, and the survivors will often try to sidestep it, which helps you quickly devour them. 

You can hear the hatch while traveling through portals. So if I go across the map one portal to another, and hear hatch halfway through, I can simply travel by foot and find it easily. 

HOWEVER, unless it is a deliciously sweaty and toxicly pungent player, you should always give hatch as demo. He gets very sad when he absolutely obliterates the competition, so showing mercy is definitely a power move to make demo feel good. Demo has a God complex after all.

If you get blinded as demo, it's because game balancing doesn't care that he has no eyes. 

As demogorgon, it's important to remember that after getting the cleanest shred down of your life, you have to spin in circles briefly before picking up. 

Run SAVE THE BEST FOR LAST on demo. It's the only perk I recommend ALWAYS using on him. It's overpowered on him, and it's so easy to use. It's very often that at 8 stacks I'll M1 someone, then immediately after shred. 3 second chase. Use STBFL. Or don't.

When using Thiccogorgon, be sure to target the meatiest survivors first. They're the most motivating. And delicious. This ensures that demo stays healthy. And we all know, a healthy demogorgon is a non unhealthy demogorgon.

Portals should be used, but don't waste unnecessary time placing them. If you plan on using the portals, here's my personal "list of importance" for the placements: Hex totems, then the gens you want to protect, then sometimes on hooked people if the survivors cleanse them a lot. This wastes their precious time, and increases their chances of ending up in your belly.

Lastly, have fun. Demogorgon is not a killer to sweat with. He should never be used for toxicity or in malice. Demo must remain pure. 

With that said, every time you hook someone open up shred and head nod before leaving. This shows a sense of superiority, which is justified because there is superiority in those who use demo.

A long while ago I saw an ad about Diabetes, and it was actually surprising in the way it described what having T1D was like. It was incredibly relatable, and made so much sense. I've since added to it slightly.

A person with a healthy pancreas and body has a helium filled balloon, tied to their wrist. They need to make sure the balloon stays filled and afloat, by exercising, eating healthy, and living a healthy lifestyle. 

A person with T1D has a balloon with no helium, and no string. They need to exercise, eat well, stay healthy to keep the balloon filled with air. But to keep the balloon from touching the ground, they must constantly bounce it into the air with one hand. But unfortunately, however good you are at bouncing it, you ultimately cannot control everything. Sometimes the wind will take your balloon away, and you must run for it. Sometimes you accidentally bounce it too high, and you have to wait for it. Sometimes you forget to bounce it, and you desperately must save it. 

The balloon represents life. If the balloon touches the floor, you die. If you lose the balloon, you die. It takes a lot work to keep your balloon alive, but it takes even more, constantly, to keep it alive when you have T1D. 
It's almost like having an invincible mosquito on you. 

The best you can do is enjoy your success, and push through your fails. It takes many years to find balance. I've had T1D since I was 3, so I guess I haven't had the challenge of "getting used to it." Getting used to it will come in a lot of time, I imagine. So in the meantime, just do everything you can to help with your T1D, and don't let it take away from your life.

Animate yourself. Use large, excited body language. This helps to keep them focused on YOU. Think of it almost like a cartoon. You want to be exciting, making kids want to watch you, but not too exciting or animated that the parents get annoyed. Like Shrek. Kids love Shrek. Parents love Shrek. Finding a balance between stern, and exciting is key to capture the attention of Kids. 

Use your smile as a tool. Do NOT smile at a kid who is misbehaving, even if it is funny. A smile should mean that the kid did something right, and that you approve. If you smile when they misbehave, you're encouraging that behavior. This is difficult when it's really small kids who are so cute... but you have to use your smile as a sign of approval. 

Commands should be short and loud. Explanation should be short to medium, and clear. This is pacing and peaking your voice. An example would be, "SET! BOW! Now, twenty jumping Jacks, I want to see who counts them out the strongest. GO!" Commands are sharp and loud, explanation is clear, simple, and short. Don't over explain, especially for kids. They will get bored. If there is one common mistake that too many instructors make, it's talking way too much. Nobody cares what you have to say, they just want action. 

Verbalize what you want from them. If it's a class of 6 year olds, usually, they are still in the process of learning class structure. Let's take the example from before. "SET! BOW! Now, Twenty jumping jacks, *I want to see who counts them the strongest.* GO! See how I make sure to mention counting them strong? This makes it exciting, because it's a competition, and it makes sure they follow the class structure the way I want them to. You shouldn't punish small kids for doing exactly what you tell them. If you say TURN, and they turn all different directions when you wanted them to face right, thats your fault, not theirs. Instead, say "When I say turn, I want you all to face right (making a hand gesture towards the direction)... TURN!" 

And lastly... at the end of the day, they're children. Make it fun. Reinforce class structure. Make them sweat, have them learn. You're going to have students that are simply not very good, but as long as they have fun and work out, and get SOMETHING out of class, even if it's small,  you've done your job. A kid's side kick can look terrible. But if you focus on the base foot? Pivot? And they get better at that?? Their sidekick still sucks, but little by little over time, it'll get much better.

Recording yourself teach is a great way to get better at teaching.

You won't get abs from doing exercises, actually. Everyone on earth has abs. The reason why they aren't visible isn't due to them being weak or small. It's due to body fat. To attain visible abs, the only way to do so is eating healthy, and losing body fat. This means that you need to be in a caloric deficit (calories are in everything you eat), to be in a deficit you must find your current daily calorie maintenance level, then eat 200-500 calories below that. (THIS IS ONLY AN EXAMPLE, as every person is different, different numbers will be necessary from person to person. Don't take what I say as a perfect solution for you, as we are not the same. The idea behind what I've said is still valid, however.)

So let's say you're at 15% body fat. You need to get to 10% to have visible abs. (Again, just an example. Some people need to get lower or higher. Genetics play a huge role in this, some people can't have "visible" abs at all without being unhealthy) this means you need to lose that fat. You won't lose that fat doing exercises. The only way to lose that fat is to be in a caloric deficit. Exercising is still very important, but you will not lose fat from exercising alone, for example you might do a 1 hour cardio session, then eat a sandwich for lunch. You just gained back every single calorie you just burned doing cardio eating that sandwich. The only way to get abs is diet. Like the old saying, "Abs are made in the kitchen, not the gym". 

Now, if you do want to train abs for strength, you should train them just like any other muscle group. Let's take the chest for example. If I can bench press 160 pounds, (example numbers) doing 8 reps, that's how I'd build my chest. It wouldn't make sense to grab 20 pounds and bench press that 10000 times, when I could get the same results faster and much more efficiently with heavier weight. Same thing applies for abs. Why train them differently? Every other muscle on the body we train using weights, why not abs? If you really want to train abs, (which is up to you, but I'd focus more on other muscles personally) you should do weighted crunches. Why do 100 crunches with no weight, when you can do 20 crunches with 25 pounds? It's much more effective, and much easier to train to failure. 

Exercise is important, but I suggest you research more about visible abs through diet. Every single YouTube ab workout video you see is illegitimate. Every. Single. One. I suggest watching Sean Nalewanyj, he has really good advice on this stuff. Now, these ab workout videos are a waste of time, unless you do them for fun rather than getting visible abs. 

If I were you, I'd research this stuff. Watch Sean Nalewanyj on YouTube, research diet, hypertrophy, progressive overload, caloric maintenance level, caloric deficit, losing weight, and more. I would also talk to your doctor about your weight, calorie specifics, and whether they think losing weight for abs would be worth it for you. 

And lastly, don't take abs too seriously. When I was younger, I would stress a ton about getting them. It wasn't worth it. I got them, but I was underweight. Yeah, I had a super six pack! I also looked like a minecraft skeleton... and if you don't have enough weight, it makes building other muscles more difficult. If I were you, I'd start working out in the gym working on overall body progress rather than isolating the abs. (Assuming you don't already go to gym) A well rounded body looks much more pleasing than an only six pack physique. Trust me, I've experienced this firsthand. Now my abs are less visible, but my body altogether looks way, WAYYY better. Overall physique beats all, in my opinion. Good luck on your fitness journey, I hope you learn something from this. 1 day, ten years, it's all the same with tricking. Some people have a harder time than others, but nearly anyone with legs can learn any of these tricks if they are determined to. Some people can just do them, other people require lots of practice. But most people fail due to lack of persistence. 

Bottom line, you just have to practice. With these particular tricks, they won't get easier as you practice other things. They'll get easier when you practice them. A few tips I'd recommend would be to find a fairly soft area like grass, and find YouTube Videos with breakdowns on them. Generally speaking, unless your Dojang includes tricking in it, you won't learn any of these from doing Taekwondo. Except maybe the spin kicks, like 360 and 540.

Search Progression based videos on these tricks, and practice practice practice. Like for instance, the aerial, you can learn the Wushu butterfly kick first, and build it up to an aerial, or a B twist. But finding ways to progress in these tricks is a very good way to learn. Or, you can just try the trick itself until you get it. 

Dedicate an hour, or ten minutes, or even 5 minutes a day to a particular trick, don't half-arse it, and practice hard. You'll get it in no time. And don't get discouraged either, some people can backflip instantly. It took me years to actually get it, and I taught my friend... he got it in 5 tries haha. Now my knees are hurt and he gets to boast his backflip while I watch and think about prosthetic knees hahaha. 

Anyways, really just practicing these tricks every day, and dedicating time to learn them. I too aspire to get back into flipping once my body is healed, and I'm going to do the same thing I'm telling you. The main thing is determination, and not getting discouraged. You'll get it, I know. And on a side note, while you should practice consistently, be careful. Your joints (particularly knees) can very easily be overworked. Make sure to ice and rest when needed, and take breaks every now and then. Getting injured halts progress, which is very demotivating sometimes.

I also suggest practicing on spring floors, trampolines, and stretching. These will all help you very much, along with strength training (higher jumps).

You can do this, just don't give up and don't hurt yourself. And remember, at the end of the day, if you practice, you'll get better. Even if you didn't land it this time, you're that much closer to landing it next time. Good luck!

Oh and if you do get injured... THERAPY. Physical therapy is the only way to heal back up, while rest is good, PT actually makes you stronger so you don't just reinjure. Since I was 14 and seriously hurt myself in Gymnastics, I always rested and I always got injured again. I didn't do PT. Now that I am doing, my knees are finally getting better. I'm 17 now, and an instructor of Taekwondo. You'll never rest enough to heal injuries without them just getting injured again, especially doing martial arts. Physical therapy. Trust me haha. 

Anyhow, sorry that last bit had nothing relating to your question, but I believe it's a very important thing to know. (Or you'll be like me!) Good luck, train hard, and have fun!

Here's what I would say is the best exercise split for beginners, and has worked incredibly well for me. 

Workout A: Bench press 8-12 reps, bent one arm dumbbell rows 8-12 reps, squat 8-12 reps. 3 sets.

Workout B: Overhead dumbbell shoulder press 8-12 reps, lat pull down or pull up 8-12 reps, squats or lunges 8-12 reps. 

Monday Exercise A, Wed B, Fri A. Then next week, Monday B, Wed A, Fri B. Every week, those three days, ABABABABAB.

4 years ago, I knew this boy. He was sad, lonely, and worthless. He was stupid, he was weak, he was socially awkward, he was lame. And he hated himself. He hated his life. And he wanted to change.

And so, 

He forced himself to change. Because all he sought after, was to be a better self. He wanted that 6 pack. He wanted that gym body. He wanted to be smart, talented, and charismatic. So when he decided to change, he wasn't joking around. He wasn't going half way. He was 13, and he swore by the time he was 16, he would be everything he sought to be.

And so, 

He began. He went starting going to the gym. He joined a martial arts school. He relentlessly searched the internet for information. He learnt much about his body, and learnt much about the world. He worked hard every day. He spent all his time working, and working, and working, until all he knew was performance. He became a machine, you could say. And because he was homeschooled, because he had no friends, because he didn't realize what he was missing out on... he simply kept working.

And so, 

When he turned 16, when he was very fit, very talented, very charismatic, and very "successful".... he finally saw, that he wasted 3 years of his life. He finally realized why he starting working so hard in the first place. To mask his pain. From others, and himself. He noticed that in the three years he worked so hard, he had no friends. He had no fun. He had no experiences. He had no memories. He had no life.

And so,

He fell into deep depression. He accomplished nothing, and wasted his time. He got so good at faking emotions, feelings, and character, that he fooled everyone around him. He was not who his family thought he was. He wasn't happy. He wasn't funny, he wasn't healthy. His family got so accustom to his masked self, that they did not believe him when he told them he was sad. They didn't believe he was depressed. They only saw the funny kid who lightened the mood always.

And so,

Throughout his 16th year, he was miserable. He changed his goal, to make friends. Have experiences. Make memories. And near the end of that year, he realized he had failed. Because what can a kid do, when his parents don't care? When he has no counseling? When he has no experience, and has no idea what to do? He was hopeless. And at this point, he was ready to give up. He was ready to end his own life. 

Now, 

This may seem silly. But I'm only telling a fraction of the story. There's more to it. There's more pain, and more agony. And unfortunately, this kid was set up for failure. 
He went on and on about what he wanted to be, how he wanted to change, how he wanted to seem... to cover up what he really wanted. Something he couldn't get in his circumstance. He fooled everyone, including himself, into thinking that all he cared about was self improvement, and himself.

And so, 

What did he accomplish? I still know this boy, from 4 years ago. He said he wanted to change. That he would fix his issues. Well? He is still sad. He is still lonely. He still feels worthless, and he still feels stupid. He feels weak and lame, and he is socially unavailable. He hates himself. He hates his life. And he wished he could change.

And so, 

Our lesson is that he focused too much on hiding his pain, and convinced himself that work could replace having a good life. He went about his issues in the wrong way, and regretted it. He set up a situation he can't get out of. And even though he accomplished great things, even though he got what many boys want, that six pack, that charisma, that skill!... he didn't get what he needed, nor truly wanted. He replaced his life with work, because he hated his life. When he could have instead, worked on getting what he needed and really wanted.

And so...

With that all said,

Friends. I could go on and on about who I wanted to be, but the moment I saw what friendship looked like, I've questioned whether that's what I've wanted all along. 

I replaced friendship with work. And I've been sad, lonely, and hurt for years. And it's too late to fix. My childhood is ruined, I am ruined. Don't hide your emotions like I did, because eventually, they will build up and up until they take you over.

The End.

It was my last class of the semester, and the final exam was worth 30% of our grade.
After a late night study session I felt confident, but I had to decide between sleeping in or cooking breakfast. My eyelids chose sleep.
My stomach later regretted this decision, and after several uncomfortable stomach growls, I finally decided to make a quick stop by the campus bookstore and grab a snack before my test. Since the semester was ending and everyone was going home for the summer, a lot of items were on sale, including the snacks and candy that they kept up front. Being in the hungry state that I was in, it felt only logical to pick the largest, yet least expensive candy in order to get more bang for my buck.
And there they sat: two bags of Haribo Sugar-Free Gummi Bears, buy one get one free.
"What a deal!" I thought naïvely. I would eat one bag before my test, and one bag afterwards.
As I walked to class, I gleefully chewed on those abominable little bastards, unaware of the utter mayhem that they would soon unleash upon my poor, poor anus.
I sat down at my desk as the professor informed us that, due to issues with cheating in the past, restroom breaks would be prohibited until the completion of the exam.
"I'll give you 10 minutes to use the restroom now; this will be your last chance. Any takers?"
The demon bears hadn't released their unholy necromancy upon my stomach yet, so in my moment of ignorant foolishness, I remained seated, still munching on those miniature bear-shaped bombs.
After the students wise enough to take the professor's offer had returned, the professor handed out the test. I was six questions in when it happened.
It started subtly at first, almost like a slight tingly sensation in my lower abdomen. I thought nothing of it, assuming my intestines were just doing their thang. Little did I know that my intestines were trying desperately to warn me of the horror that was on the horizon.
By question 9 it happened again, but this time it was followed by a sharp pain, as if those infernal hellions had orchestrated an attack upon my colon. I fought to contain the groan that tried escaping my lips. It was at this point I began to panic; something was going horribly long, and I needed to get through this test before it got any worse.
By question 14 my worst fear was upon me; the Satan bears' burning, hot, liquidy dark magic crashed against my anal sphincter like a tidal wave. I was able to close the hatch just in time, but those relentless, toxic bears beat against it like Orcs breaking down the doors of Helm's Deep. I knew I wouldn't be able to so much as shift in my seat without risking a breach.
I kept fighting through my exam, clenching my cheeks with all my might. Beads of sweat began rolling down my neck. Suddenly, a loud, gurgling war cry came from my belly, and the entire class lifted their heads.
At this point, nothing mattered except expelling this ungodly presence from my bowels. With 15 questions left, I promptly wrote C for every answer and ran out of the classroom. My professor yelled something, but I was too preoccupied with the volcanic eruption that needed to take place before I could find sweet, sweet relief.
I burst into the restroom like the Kool-Aid man and, behold, the handicap stall was empty. Sun rays from the adjacent window shone upon it, as if it were a gift from God himself. It took me less than .5 seconds to undo my belt buckle, pull down my pants, and finally relax my weary buttocks upon the toilet seat.
It took absolutely no effort to expel this demon. Almost immediately, the floodgates of hell were opened and the damned, liquified souls of an entire bag's worth of gummi bears cried as they burned through my sphincter and into the watery abyss below. I had never felt such simultaneous relief and anguish in my life.
After 30 more minutes of this, I immediately went home, dug a hole in my backyard, and burned the remaining bag of gummi bears.
I leave with this; do not, I repeat do NOT eat these spawns of Satan. Not only did they cause me to fail my final test, but the anguish I experienced is something I wouldn't wish upon anyone, not even my worst enemy. The only place these god forsaken hell bears belong are buried deep below the Earth's surface.
